{{Short description|Shinto sect}}
{{Nihongo|'''Shinto Taiseikyo'''|神道大成教}} is one of the [[Sect Shinto|thirteen Shinto sects]].<ref name="日本国語大辞典百科事典マイヘティア-2022a">{{Cite web |last=日本国語大辞典,百科事典マイペディア |first=日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ),デジタル大辞泉,精選版 |title=神道大成教とは |url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%A5%9E%E9%81%93%E5%A4%A7%E6%88%90%E6%95%99-538590 |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=コトバンク |language=ja}}</ref><ref name="enpediarxyjp-2022a">{{Cite web |title=神道大成教 - Enpedia |url=https://enpedia.rxy.jp/wiki/%E7%A5%9E%E9%81%93%E5%A4%A7%E6%88%90%E6%95%99 |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=enpedia.rxy.jp}}{{User-generated source|date=January 2024}}</ref>{{User-generated source|date=January 2024}}<ref>文化庁編 2017, p.4-6</ref> It was founded by [[Hirayama Seisai]] (1815–1890)<ref name="日本国語大辞典百科事典マイヘティア-2022a" /> and is considered a form of [[Confucian Shinto]].<ref name="日本国語大辞典百科事典マイヘティア-2022a" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Forms of Shinto |url=https://www.myss.com/free-resources/world-religions/shinto/the-forms-of-shinto/ |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=Caroline Myss |date=8 July 2015 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Kyōha Shintō {{!}} Japanese religion {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kyoha-Shinto |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=www.britannica.com |language=en}}</ref>

== History ==
[[Hirayama Seisai]] was involved in diplomatic negotiations as a senior vassal of the [[Tokugawa shogunate|Shogunate]] at the end of the [[Edo period]].<ref name="shindenboojp-2022a">{{Cite web |title=神道大成教 - SHINDEN |url=http://shinden.boo.jp/wiki/%E7%A5%9E%E9%81%93%E5%A4%A7%E6%88%90%E6%95%99 |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=shinden.boo.jp}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=「神道大成教」の意味や使い方 Weblio辞書 |url=https://www.weblio.jp/content/%E7%A5%9E%E9%81%93%E5%A4%A7%E6%88%90%E6%95%99 |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=www.weblio.jp}}</ref> At the beginning of the [[Meiji Restoration]], he turned to Shinto.<ref name="enpediarxyjp-2022a" />{{User-generated source|date=January 2024}} He became a Shinto teacher in 1872, and rallied for independence as a [[Sect Shinto|Shinto Sect]] in 1879, which was gained in 1882.<ref name="井上順孝-1991a">井上順孝『教派神道の形成』（弘文堂　1991年）

朝日日本歴史人物事典（朝日新聞出版）<!-- uncertain origin from Japanese Wikipedia article https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%B9%B3%E5%B1%B1%E7%9C%81%E6%96%8E --></ref><ref>Sugada 1994, p.178-180

Masaaki Sugata "Old Shindo Revives" Tachibana Publishing, 1994

菅田正昭『古神道は甦る』橘出版、1994年</ref><ref name="enpediarxyjp-2022a" />{{User-generated source|date=January 2024}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=神道大成教（しんとうたいせいきょう）の意味 - goo国語辞書 |url=https://dictionary.goo.ne.jp/word/%E7%A5%9E%E9%81%93%E5%A4%A7%E6%88%90%E6%95%99/ |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=goo辞書 |language=ja}}</ref> During his tenure as president, [[Mitake-kyo]] also gained independence.<ref name="井上順孝-1991a" />

After [[World War II]], it became independent from the Sect Shinto federation alongside [[Tenrikyo]].<ref name="tudoi2">Inori and Tsudoi: A History of the 100th Anniversary of the Formation of the Shinto Federation of Churches, 1996, pp. 10-12.</ref> Still, in 1995, the president attended a [[Sect Shinto]] event the "100th Anniversary of the Formation of the Federation of Shinto Churches".<ref name="100ani">{{Cite news |date=1995-09-05 |script-title=ja:結成100周年の記念式典 |script-work=ja:産経新聞}}</ref>

== Shrines ==
Shrines of Shinto Taiseikyo include<ref name="shindenboojp-2022a" />

* Tenshozan Shrine – Yugawara Town, Ashigarashimo District, Kanagawa Prefecture<ref name="shindenboojp-2022a" />
* Tenshozan Shrine branch shrine<ref name="shindenboojp-2022a" />
* Hirayama Seisai Tomb – located in Yanaka Cemetery<ref name="shindenboojp-2022a" />
